findings.checklist_item: State explicitly whether the dynamic re-add is an amend of the imported tip commit (count preserved) or an appended commit (count+1), and reconcile that choice with AC-1's commit-count-equality assertion.
evidence: Plan: 'the rewritten HEAD tree byte-identical after the dynamic re-add'
AC-1: 'the rewritten branch commit count equals the measured old-tip commit count'
AC-4: 'After dynamic re-add, rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree} exactly equals rev-parse <old-tip>^{tree}'

The re-add restores four .bridge_state/ files that the filter stripped from every revision, so it must add tree content back at the tip — but the plan never states whether this is a fresh commit (count+1) or an amend of the imported tip (count preserved).
findings.finding: The plan asserts both that the rewritten commit count equals the old-tip commit count (AC-1) and that the rewritten HEAD tree is byte-identical to old-tip after a 'dynamic re-add' (AC-4), but never specifies whether the dynamic re-add is a new commit appended on top of the imported tip or an amend/replacement of the imported tip commit. If it is a new commit, the count becomes old-tip+1 and AC-1 fails; if it is an amend, the plan must say so and describe how the tip's parent/topology is preserved.
findings.location: §Why stock plumbing / Required corrections item 3 / AC-1 and AC-4
scenarios: Implementer appends a re-add commit to satisfy tree-identity, then AC-1's commit-count-equality assertion fails on the scratch clone.
Implementer amends the tip to satisfy AC-1 but the topology/parent handling is unspecified, risking a divergent tip shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the re-add as an in-place amend of the imported tip commit (reusing its message, author, and single/merge parent set) so the tree becomes byte-identical to old-tip while the total commit count and merge-commit count remain equal to old-tip; note this explicitly next to AC-1 and AC-4.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `grep` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The plan asserts a <=150 MB pack-size acceptance criterion for a fresh unfiltered clone of the rewritten branch, but never accounts for the remote tag `pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` that the plan's own cited session log (1cb6-d553-6565-49b4, item [3]) says pins 22,317 commits / 63 MB and 'MUST be deleted or the reclaim lands at 167 MB not 94 MiB'. A scratch clone that still fetches that tag's reachable objects would exceed the ceiling, so the asserted pack-size capability is not achievable as described without a stated tag-removal/exclusion step.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'A fresh unfiltered clone of the rewritten branch has pack size at most 150 MB'; Required corrections / Publication boundary
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Required correction and a companion AC: before recording old-tip, delete or exclude the `pre-heal-a118-*` tag (and clone the scratch with `--no-tags` or prune tag refs), and assert no such tag ref is reachable in the rewritten scratch clone prior to the pack-size measurement.
